observations: Engine block with a silver-colored alternator attached.
The engine appears to be used, with visible dirt and grime on the casing.
A green sticker is visible on the alternator, but the text is illegible.
The engine is surrounded by other mechanical parts, suggesting it may be a used or scrap unit.

risks.risk: The engine may not be a 2.0L unit as claimed.
risks.proof: A photo of the engine identification plate (usually on the engine block or the alternator).

risks.risk: The engine may be a used or scrap unit rather than a genuine replacement part.
risks.proof: A photo of the engine with a handwritten note showing the purchase date.

risks.risk: The alternator may be faulty or have a different capacity than the engine.
risks.proof: A photo of the alternator's specification sticker.

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Photo of the engine identification plate showing the engine size (e.g., 2.0L).
Photo of the alternator's specification sticker.
Photo of the seller's text to confirm the claim.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
